## TL;DR

The review card now bases its green “ready to finish” treatment on the shared landability result used by the task drawer. While the result is missing or blocked, the card describes the blocker, dims and disables Move to done, and refreshes the result while the review card is visible. An active post-review check run also prevents the ready state. The drawer’s Move to done action now follows the same readiness rule, including active checks. Amber and red review verdicts no longer style the card action as the primary green action.

The implementation leaves close-out processing unchanged: a permitted click still calls the existing complete-task action and enqueues the normal pipeline. A checks-running board shot is declared through RepoOS using the new `card:reviewChecksRunning` fixture.

## Work and rationale

`TaskCard.vue` previously derived readiness from the review report, agent state, and close-out pipeline. It did not read the landability record that `TaskDrawer.vue` obtains from the server. The card now reads `repo.landableFor(task.id)`, the same shared store field the drawer reads, and requests the server result when a review card appears. It retries while readiness remains blocked, at five-second intervals, and stops polling once readiness is green. Hidden tabs do not make polling requests; a visibility change re-evaluates the card so it resumes when the board becomes visible again.

The card’s ready predicate now requires a green review verdict, no running review or engineer, no stale handoff, no close-out, a green landability result, and no running check run. A blocked result selects its first failing check and uses its details in the card title. The hint distinguishes a running check from a failed preflight, while an as-yet-unloaded result says that merge readiness is being checked. The existing disabled footer treatment provides the dimmed inert style, with the blocker as the action title. The done action only receives its green footer treatment when the ready predicate is true.

The drawer now disables Move to done until landability is green and while its shared check, local waiting, local slot, or handoff signals show checks in progress. Its title tells the user whether checks are still running or merge readiness has not passed. These are display and action-state changes; neither the request endpoint nor the close-out pipeline was modified.

Component coverage now exercises green readiness, running and failing preflight, amber and red review verdicts, the drawer’s blocked and green landability states, and a live post-review check run. Older tests that intended to test the green-ready experience were updated to seed green landability, including the move-to-done success path and stale needs-input card case. The screenshot fixture seeds a green reviewer report alongside an explicitly blocked “Checks running” preflight, so the capture demonstrates the disagreement state this task fixes.

## Approaches tried

I first confirmed the documented contract in `docs/close-out-pipeline.md`: `repoos landable` is the read-only merge-readiness answer, and the drawer displays that same result. I kept the implementation on the presentation side of that contract rather than changing validation or close-out behavior. I then checked the existing store and drawer loading path and reused the landability store/API instead of creating a second card-specific readiness model.

The first scoped remote check exposed legacy fixtures that assumed a green verdict alone should enable the action. I updated those fixtures to state their intended precondition explicitly. The next run exposed two additional tests that performed a successful close-out from the drawer or asserted a ready card while leaving landability unset; those received green landability fixtures. The affected tests then passed locally before the final remote check.

## Challenges and blockers

The first final-tree upload encountered an incremental-bundle base mismatch on the remote runner. RepoOS retried with a full bundle, verified the intended commit, and completed validation. The initial test run also failed on the assumptions described above; those were test setup gaps caused by the new readiness contract, not changes to close-out behavior. The focused affected tests passed after correction.

## Key learnings

A review verdict answers whether the reviewer approved the work; it does not prove that the branch can merge at this moment. The UI should make that distinction explicit and consume the same server-computed readiness value wherever it presents “ready to finish.” Tests that create a ready review state should seed both a green verdict and green landability. Check-run progress is a separate live signal from the preflight result, so both card and drawer must account for it when enabling the human action.

Final verification: `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passed on the final implementation. The remote changed-path suite passed, as did local formatting/lint, build, contrast audits, and UI smoke. The focused card, drawer, and shot-fixture suites passed locally after the last fixture corrections.
